entry.title: MacOS Style Dock 1.0
entry.content:
MacOS Style Dock

Turns the Windows 11 taskbar into a dock with the look and feel of macOS, while it keeps working the way Windows does. It restyles the real taskbar rather than replacing it, so pinned apps, jump lists, thumbnails, dragging files onto apps and rearranging your apps all work as usual. (Unlike "Taskbar Dock Animation", which magnifies the stock taskbar's icons, and "Mac Island & Dock", which replaces the taskbar with a separate dock window.)

The look

  • A frosted glass dock. Your icons sit on a rounded plate of blurred, tinted glass with a thin edge, floating just above the bottom of the screen, in place of the taskbar's flat background. It's dark, light, or follows your Windows theme.
  • Bigger icons, no boxes. Icons are shown larger, without the square highlight Windows draws behind them on hover or for the active app.
  • Sharp at any size. Icons are loaded at the size they're shown at when fully magnified, so they stay crisp as they grow.
  • Running indicators. A small dot under each running app, just above the bottom of the dock.
  • Dividers. Thin lines separate Start, Task View and File Explorer from your other apps, and your apps from the Recycle Bin.
  • A tidier system tray. The clock, notifications and tray icons on the right keep a fixed size and position, with even margins from the screen edges, whatever size the dock is.

How it works

  • Magnification. Icons grow as the pointer passes over them, smoothly falling off with distance, and push their neighbors aside. As on a Mac, the dock grows from one end: with the pointer right of its middle, its left end stays put and its right end moves, and the other way around. The dock shrinks back as soon as the pointer leaves it.
  • Over your windows. Maximized windows reach down to the top of the dock, and magnified icons rise over them. Windows still keeps the dock's own strip of the screen free.
  • A fixed order. Start comes first, then Task View, then File Explorer, a divider, and the rest of your apps. Whenever File Explorer is pinned or open, it keeps its spot next to the divider and can't be dragged elsewhere; your other apps can be rearranged as usual.
  • Jump lists in the right place. Right-click menus open above the icon you clicked.
  • A Recycle Bin at the right end of the dock, using Windows' own icon, which shows whether it's empty or full. Click it to open it, drag files onto it to delete them (they can be restored), or right-click it to open or empty it.

Settings

  • Dock Panel: the size of the icons and dock, and the dock's color (System, Dark or Light), tint and blur.
  • Magnification: how much icons grow, how far from the pointer they grow, how long the animation takes, and whether icons magnify over maximized windows. With that turned off, the space above the dock is kept free for magnified icons instead, so maximized windows get a little less of the screen.
  • Dock Items: the divider after File Explorer, and the Recycle Bin.

Compatibility

  • Windows 11 only, with the taskbar at the bottom of the screen.
  • x64 PCs only for now; ARM64 isn't supported yet.
  • The "Small taskbar buttons" setting isn't supported.
  • Leave Windows' "Automatically hide the taskbar" setting off. While "Magnify over windows" is on, the mod turns it on behind the scenes (and keeps the taskbar from hiding), and puts it back as it was when the setting or the mod is turned off. If the mod can't put it back, for example when Windhawk is uninstalled while Explorer isn't running, turn it off yourself in Windows' taskbar settings.
  • Icons are loaded at high resolution on Windows 11 with the October 2024 update (KB5044384) or later. On older builds, magnified icons are blurrier.
  • Not designed to be used with other taskbar mods. In particular, it sets the taskbar's height and icon size, lays out and animates its icons itself, and places their right-click menus, so don't combine it with "Taskbar height and icon size", "Taskbar Dock Animation", "Taskbar Dock Animation Plus", "Mac Island & Dock", "Taskbar Multirow" or "Start button always on the left".
  • If Windows' Smart App Control is on, it blocks this mod (as it does all Windhawk mods), because the mod is compiled on your PC and isn't signed.

Credits

The taskbar height code is based on m417z's "Taskbar height and icon size" mod. The way it handles dragging icons and places right-click menus follows his "Taskbar Multirow" mod, and the way it keeps the taskbar shown follows his "Taskbar auto-hide when maximized" mod (all GPL-3.0).

entry.title: CoverTabby 0.22.14
entry.content:
CoverTabby

Replaces the alt+tab with a modded kind of the stardock alt tabby's layout.

By LTHC (LoreTheHolyChip). Version 0.22.14.

Win+Tab integration is experimental and disabled by default. Alt+Tab remains enabled. Explorer forwards Alt+Tab to the switcher running in Windhawk’s own tool process. No separate application needs to be installed.

Credits: caliberda (MIT-licensed Alt+Tab Flip 3D renderer), Lone (touchpad integration), and the Simple Window Switcher contributors (HID parsing). Renderer: https://github.com/ramensoftware/windhawk-mods/blob/main/mods/alt-tab-flip-3d.wh.cpp Touchpad source by Lone (Louis047): https://github.com/ramensoftware/windhawk-mods/pull/5396 Simple Window Switcher credits the GPLv2 upstream sws by valinet: https://github.com/valinet/sws CoverTabby is distributed under GPL-2.0-only; MIT terms remain applicable to the renderer portions. License texts are included below in the source.

Styles

| Style | Preview | | --- | --- | | Tiles — Windowed | | | Tiles — Fullscreen | | | Normal — Windowed | | | Normal — Fullscreen | | | Icons only | | | No thumbnail | | | Text only | | | Search | | | Windows 10/11 Enchanted | |

These screenshots were captured using a macro. The same macro can generate fresh screenshots whenever I update CoverTabby.

thanks for using my mod :D

Windows 11 supported; Windows 10 1607 (build 14393) and newer are experimental and use the built-in Segoe MDL2 Assets icon font. On Windows 10 builds earlier than 20348, live-captured windows can display a yellow capture border because those builds cannot disable it. The desktop overview's virtual-desktop management requires Windows 11; on Windows 10, those controls are unavailable.

Pressing the top grip quickly reveals the real window without starting a drag. Move while holding to drag it with its native decorations and a short centered popup animation. Resizable windows shrink to the preview size while the remaining interface fades out. Releasing the mouse stops the drag. A simple click still switches windows. Canceling before dragging restores the window's original size, position and minimized/maximized state. Minimized and maximized windows are restored to a movable window before the drag begins, including minimized windows that would normally restore maximized. Drag from the top area of a preview: a standard Windows title bar or system menu is not required. Clicking elsewhere selects the window. Custom title bars and borderless application windows keep their own decorations. Fixed-size windows keep their native size while moving. Minimized windows show a card matching the Windows light/dark theme, with a top drag grip and a restore hint. The app icon remains in the icon strip below. If CoverTabby previously captured the window, its last preview is kept in memory and shown blurred and darkened while minimized. Holding the top grip reveals the restored real window with sharp content; moving starts the held drag. Windows without a saved preview use the regular theme-colored minimized card.

Modes

  • Full fills the monitor. Background Style chooses Blur, Opaque or Transparent.
  • Windowed uses a compact centered popup. Windowed Scale resizes the entire popup.

Colors, fonts and rounded corners follow Windows 11 automatically.

Enable Show Desktop Card to keep a Desktop item at the end of the carousel. Selecting it uses Windows' native Show Desktop action.

Language

Language is detected at every start: Italian for an Italian Windows display language, English otherwise. Window titles and custom desktop names keep their original text.

Features

Live previews, application icons, grouped windows, Pin / Unpin, hover close controls, reflections and smooth animations. Settings cover only the essentials. Hover Behavior offers Show Title, Select Window or None for unselected windows. Opening uses a quick stationary fade. On normal selection, the selected preview smoothly resizes and returns to the real window position, starting fast and slowing down at the end. The real window remains visible beneath the topmost overlay throughout this return animation. The background fades in place while the remaining previews, icons and controls slide down and fade. Dragging keeps following the mouse instead. Hover Animation offers None, Lift, Enlarge or Lift + Enlarge. It is disabled for unselected windows when Hover Behavior is None. Click a preview to activate it.

Search

While CoverTabby is open, press Alt+S, type a window title or application name, then press Enter. Search Bar Scale changes the bar, icon and text together. Width adapts automatically. Disable Search Bar to remove its reserved space and center the content. Search is unavailable in Windowed mode and Tiles.

Virtual desktops

In the Win+Tab overview, desktop cards include the Windows taskbar on the current desktop when capture is available, with a themed app bar as the fallback on that desktop only. Other desktops do not show a taskbar. A left-side app dock offers animated selection and hover labels; minimized windows use the separate upper dock. Desktop rename keeps the text caret and animates new letters with a quick fade, upward overshoot and smooth settling. Drag an app preview or dock icon onto another desktop card to move the window there, keeping its original position and size. A simple click activates it. Drag it away from the desktop cards to take the real window onto the current desktop. Maximized and minimized windows stay unchanged until movement begins, then restore to their normal size and follow the held pointer.

Hover the selected preview to reveal the green desktop icon and label alongside Pin and Close. Click it to open CoverTabby's own desktop picker, then choose a desktop to move the window there without changing its position or size. The current desktop stays active. Use the mouse wheel to scroll the list when there are many desktops.

Process information

CPU, RAM and GPU appear below the selected application's icon and refresh approximately every 1.5 seconds while the selection is stable. These are metrics for the process owning the selected window, not its child processes. RAM shows the working set in MB/GB; its color uses the percentage of physical RAM. GPU reports the busiest GPU engine for that process, or N/A when counters are unavailable. Usage colors are green up to 10%, white below 35%, yellow below 50%, orange up to 75%, and red above 75%. Hover the selected preview to see relative process age at the top right, such as Opened 5 minutes ago. This is process age, not window age. The skull button beside Close kills the owning process, including its other windows, after a second confirming click within four seconds. Unsaved work will be lost. Close continues to request normal application closure.

Icon controls

Hover an app icon for a small smooth lift, zoom and Windows accent background. Right-click an icon or preview to open CoverTabby's animated menu: Close, Kill, and Pin/Unpin. These actions target the clicked window without changing selection. Click outside or press Escape to dismiss. Releasing Alt still closes CoverTabby. The menu is rendered by CoverTabby and uses Segoe Fluent Icons.

Navigation

Alt+Tab cycles forward; Shift+Alt+Tab or Alt+` cycles backward. The first press selects the next or previous window relative to the active window, including when pinned windows change the list order. With Group Windows enabled, Up/Down selects a window in the current application. Windows from the same application stay consecutive. Switching between them moves the stack vertically; Left/Right changes applications horizontally. Mouse selection and wheel navigation are also supported.

Performance and background

Background Style offers Blur, Opaque and Transparent in Full and Windowed. Transparent Background Opacity controls the tint without applying blur. Background During Energy Saver automatically switches to Opaque or Transparent while Windows saves energy; Keep Selected Background disables this override.

The selected preview starts first. Other live previews start progressively, and opening waits at most 45 ms for the selected capture after startup. Desktop blur is captured at up to 960 pixels on its longest side. Preview Cache reuses up to twelve 512-pixel snapshots (384 during Energy Saver), updated gradually only while the switcher is open. When closed, captures stop except for a window currently being held and dragged. Dragging, search, groups, controls and animations remain available. VSync is always enabled: the render loop waits on DXGI frame availability with a one-frame queue and has no fixed 60 FPS cap. The actual rate follows the display compositor and available GPU performance.

Precision touchpad

Three fingers starting in the lower third and moving upward open CoverTabby. Continuing that same stroke sideways navigates. Starting in the middle third and moving upward requests normal closure of the selected window while CoverTabby is open. Swipe downward to dismiss; a short three-finger tap selects the current window. Holding still gives animated press feedback. Existing touchpad mouse-click/hold dragging stays available.

Touchpad from Modern Window Switcher — Lone. HID parsing adapted from the downloaded Simple Window Switcher 3.0 source. The gesture controller is used where supported; older Windows builds may require setting native three-finger swipe/tap actions to Nothing in Windows touchpad settings to prevent duplicate system actions. Disable Precision Touchpad Gestures to stop listening to touchpad reports.

Desktop overview

Hold to Preview is optional and disabled by default. In thumbnail styles, hold Alt on the same selection for five seconds to enlarge its native-resolution live capture to fit the monitor without stretching. Tab slides the enlarged image left; releasing Alt returns it toward the real window. Minimized previews also enlarge; two seconds after reaching full size, their minimized message changes to a playful message.

While CoverTabby is open, type a letter to focus Search and filter immediately without changing the selected style. Search must be enabled for the current mode. Press Enter to activate a result or Escape to cancel.

Win+Tab opens the optional desktop overview. Further Tab presses while holding Win select the next desktop; Shift+Tab selects the previous one. Hold Win to Keep Desktop Overview Open is enabled by default: releasing Win activates the selection. Disable it to leave the overview open; touchpad opening remains persistent. Beginning a rename leaves hold mode so typing is possible. Three quick three-finger taps toggle between windows and desktops while CoverTabby is open. A single tap is confirmed after a short 340 ms recognition window. Hover a desktop to reveal its centered name and Alt+Tab-style controls. Rename uses a blue pencil button, Delete uses a red trash button, and their labels expand on hover; Desktop 1 cannot be deleted. Rename supports Enter to save and Escape to cancel. The + button after the last desktop creates a new desktop; deleting a desktop moves its windows to the previous desktop. Desktop cards have equal sizes, stay flat and slide horizontally. Desktop overview always fills the monitor. Panels share Alt+Tab's theme-aware material and controls. Alt+Tab and Alt+` select the next/previous open app on the selected desktop; releasing Alt activates it. Left/right arrows select desktops, and clicking an app or pressing Enter focuses it. Minimized apps appear as an icon dock in a rounded top panel; titles appear only when hovering an icon. The app list follows the shell switcher visibility flag and refreshes while open, excluding retained hidden app windows. Live window captures are loaded incrementally for the selected and adjacent desktops (up to four extra captures, two in energy saver); unavailable frames use saved previews or icons and titles. Click or tap to activate the selected desktop; Escape or a downward swipe cancels. Each open HWND is shown as a separate fitted tile inside its desktop card; windows from the same application are never grouped or stacked together in this view.

Each card shows its wallpaper and window layout. Active-window content is live; other desktops reuse available snapshots. Windows without cached content show their application icon and title. At most three small wallpaper textures are loaded at once. Windows' internal desktop contracts vary between builds; unsupported builds show an availability message.

entry.title: Secondary Monitor Pin 1.1
entry.content:
Secondary Monitor Pin

Automatically pins windows that are placed on a secondary monitor so that they are shown on all virtual desktops, the same as choosing Show this window on all desktops from the window's title bar context menu.

When a window moves back to the primary monitor it is unpinned again, but only if this mod was the one that pinned it. Windows that were pinned manually are left untouched.

The mod runs as a tool mod in a dedicated process, so it does not inject into explorer.exe. It only talks to the virtual desktop manager when a window changes monitors, when a new window appears or when a window closes, which keeps the number of shell calls low and keeps switching virtual desktops smooth. A timer polls for monitor changes that the window event hooks do not report, such as Win+Shift+arrow, programmatic moves and display changes.

Windows that are on another virtual desktop are pinned too, so the secondary-monitor windows of every desktop end up shown together on all desktops.

Notes

  • Uses undocumented Windows virtual desktop interfaces, which may change with future Windows updates.
  • Works on Windows 10 and Windows 11.
  • Do not run this mod together with another tool that also pins windows across virtual desktops, as two implementations competing over the same shell interfaces can cause issues.

entry.title: AltTab Mouse Focus 1.1
entry.content:
AltTab Mouse Focus

Moves the mouse cursor to the center of the window that gets focused after switching windows with Alt+Tab.

  • Only acts on Alt+Tab. Clicking, other keyboard shortcuts or focus changes made by other programs do not move the cursor.
  • The cursor is moved once the Alt key is released, after the window switcher closes.
  • Ignores system overlays (desktop, taskbar, the Alt+Tab switcher).
  • Moves the cursor as soon as the selected window receives focus (EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND), instead of polling.
  • Works with multiple monitors: the cursor is centered on the monitor where the focused window is.

The mod runs as a tool mod in a dedicated process, so it does not inject into explorer.exe.

entry.title: Windows 7/8.1 UAC Recreation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 7/8.1 UAC Recreation

This mod recreates the Windows 7 and 8.1 classic UAC interface on Windows 10 and 11. It changes only the presentation: Windows retains control of consent, authentication, and the secure desktop.

Features

  • Four themes: Windows 7 Basic, custom Aero, Windows 8.1, and Windows 10 (1507–1607).
  • It restores the native prompt if the recreation fails; never makes an elevation decision.
  • It leaves system files, settings, and credential prompts untouched.
  • It matches the banner and shield to Windows' publisher verdict.
  • Ithows the requesting program's icon and native prompt details when available.

Emergency shortcut

Press Ctrl+Shift+F10 to close the recreated dialog and return to the native prompt without approving or denying the request.

Themes

Windows 7 (Basic)

Windows 7 Aero

Windows 8.1

Windows 10 (1507–1607)

Installation

Windhawk excludes consent.exe by default. To enable the mod:

  1. Open Settings → Advanced settings → More advanced settings.
  2. Add consent.exe to the Process inclusion list.
  3. Install and enable the mod.

Without this change, the mod has no effect.

Settings

| Setting | Description | |---|---| | Dialog skin | Choose one of the four themes. | | Replace the UAC prompt | Replace the prompt or observe it and log events. | | Which apps get the Classic UAC prompt | Apply to all apps, only listed apps, or all except listed apps. | | App list | Semicolon-separated application names for the filter above. | | Button style | Use the system button or the mod's Aero-style button. | | Which shield is shown | Choose automatic, verified, question, or exclamation. | | Banner colour | Choose automatic, blue, yellow, or red; manual choices can only make the prompt more cautious. | | The Windows prompt, while the Windows 7 one is on screen | Move the native prompt off-screen or hide it. | | Read the elevation request | Read request details to show the app icon and "File origin". | | How long to wait for the prompt | Wait time, in milliseconds, before leaving the native prompt unchanged. | | Watchdog | Close the recreated dialog after this many seconds without a response. | | Panic hotkey | Shortcut to restore the native prompt; default: Ctrl+Shift+F10. | | Extra Yes/No key | Optional Alt+letter shortcut forwarded to the original prompt. | | Debug log | Record mod activity. | | Write a diagnostics dump | Write diagnostics; the mod runs in observation mode. | | Write the raw elevation request to the log | Log the raw request, which may include file and user names. | | How the prompt is found | Choose desktop watchers (recommended), polling, or hook only. |

Behavior and limitations

  • The banner follows the native publisher row. The shield follows the selected theme and Windows' verdict; the mod never upgrades an unknown or unverified publisher to verified.
  • Publisher checks use the file's Authenticode signature or its Windows catalog when applicable. The native verdict is not overridden.
  • Regedit is shown by its localized name only after Windows confirms the system file's signature.
  • Details that cannot be read from the native prompt are omitted, not guessed.
  • A XAML candidate without a Win32 edit control may be moved off-screen briefly during UI Automation classification.
  • Logs and diagnostic files can contain prompt text, command lines, file names, and user names. Enable them only when needed.

Tested systems

The modification has been tested on the following systems:

  • Windows 10 21H2
  • Windows 11 24H2
  • Windows 11 25H2

Credits

  • AdministratoX — Windows 11 24H2/25H2 testing
  • Microsoft — Documentation
  • m417z — Technical reference and review

Reporting issues

If there are anomalies, please report them to the author. It is recommended to include the debug log and, if needed, the diagnostic file.

entry.title: Sticky Notes: Alt+Tab group 1.1.1
entry.content:
Sticky Notes: Alt+Tab group

Keep multiple Microsoft Sticky Notes windows from filling the Alt+Tab switcher.

  • Show one representative Sticky Notes window in Alt+Tab.
  • Switch to Sticky Notes to bring all its open windows on the current virtual desktop forward together.
  • Minimized notes are restored; closed notes are not opened.
  • Switching from another application by clicking a note or its taskbar button also brings the open notes forward.
  • Use compact Sticky Notes previews, with a default maximum source size of 260 by 160 pixels while preserving the aspect ratio.
  • Other shell views that use the same thumbnail factory can also use this compact source size. The shell controls the final display scale.
  • Matching uses the note window's extended frame bounds.
  • Keep note contents, window sizes, positions, and ownership unchanged.

Compatibility

  • Windows 11, x64, with the standard XAML Alt+Tab switcher.
  • Locally tested on Windows 11 25H2, build 26200.9457, Windhawk 1.7.3, and Microsoft Sticky Notes 6.1.4.0.
  • Other Windows builds and the newer OneNote-based Sticky Notes experience have not been tested.
  • Uses private shell symbols, which may change after Windows updates.
  • Tested alongside Alt+Tab per monitor 1.2 with its cursor-monitor filter.
  • That mod's monitor filtering still applies. Notes restored after selection can be on any monitor on the current virtual desktop.
  • Disabling this mod restores the normal switcher behavior.
  • Do not enable both a local copy and the catalog version simultaneously.

Settings

  • Preview maximum width / height: maximum reported Sticky Notes thumbnail source dimensions. Values at or below zero use the defaults (260 / 160).

Credits

The Alt+Tab visibility-filtering approach is adapted from Alt+Tab per monitor by L3r0y and Alt+Tab: Hide ghost windows by David Trapp (CherryDT). Their MIT notices are retained below.

entry.title: What When Where Notes 1.3.2
entry.content:
What When Where Notes

A customizable desktop note overlay for Windows, powered by Windhawk. Organize reminders in three editable parts: What - When - Where.

Screenshots

Task overview and status indicators

Custom colors and row highlighting

Edit notes directly on the desktop

Right-click color and transparency menu

Task status indicators

Click the colored circle next to a task to change its state:

  • ⚪ Gray — Open: The task has not been started.
  • 🔴 Red — In Progress: Work on the task is underway.
  • 🟢 Green — Completed: What, When and Where are struck through.

Cycle: ⚪ Open → 🔴 In Progress → 🟢 Completed → ⚪ Open. Each task's status is saved across Windhawk restarts.

Features

  • Up to 14 numbered note rows with independently editable What, When and Where fields.
  • Optional centered title, adjustable fonts, spacing and colors.
  • Three status states for each row: gray (open), red (in progress), and green (done). Completed notes are struck through.
  • Add rows, remove the last row, or delete a selected row.
  • Move the overlay with a configurable drag-mode hotkey.
  • Adjustable transparency and note color; optional always-on-top behavior.
  • Saved notes, row statuses, position and display preferences persist across restarts.

Using the notes

  • Click a What, When or Where field to edit it. Press Enter to save or Esc to cancel. Leaving the edit field also saves.
  • Click + to add a row (up to the configured maximum) or - to remove the last row.
  • Click the X next to a row to delete that row. At least one row is kept.
  • Click a status circle to cycle through open, in progress and done.
  • Right-click the overlay to open the color and transparency menu.
  • Mouse wheel over the overlay to scale it in 10% steps (20% to 320%); middle-click to reset the scale.
  • Press Ctrl+Alt+N by default to toggle drag mode, then drag the overlay with the left mouse button. Press the hotkey again to exit drag mode.

Configuration

Open Settings to customize the initial position, always-on-top mode, title, the three default note fields, separators, maximum row count, fonts, colors, default transparency, default scale, and the drag hotkey.

Note: Existing edited notes and saved display preferences are stored separately from the initial defaults. Changing a default does not automatically overwrite previously saved note rows. A previously dragged position is preserved when changing unrelated options. Editing X/Y settings explicitly moves the overlay to those new coordinates.

Technical information

  • Designed for Windows / Windhawk.
  • Runs as a Windhawk tool mod, using a dedicated windhawk.exe helper process.
  • The overlay is implemented with the Windows API and GDI.
  • Source code and license: GitHub repository.

Project background and relation to Easy Notes

This mod is an independent Windows/Windhawk implementation inspired by the original ToDoLite / What When Where Rainmeter project by the same author: https://forum.rainmeter.net/viewtopic.php?t=42543#p215957

Unlike free-form desktop sticky notes, this mod displays a structured three-field task list (What / When / Where) with distinct Open / In Progress / Completed states. The current version is intentionally focused on that workflow.

Author

SilverAmd

entry.title: Explorer Properties Button 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Properties Button

Adds a Properties button to the Windows 11 File Explorer command bar, between the Delete and Sort buttons. Clicking it opens the properties dialog of the current selection:

  • Multiple selection - opens the combined properties dialog, just like the context menu's Properties entry.
  • Virtual locations - This PC, Recycle Bin, Quick Access and other items without a filesystem path work too.
  • No selection (configurable) - shows the properties of the current folder, or does nothing.

The dialog opens via fast shell APIs (SHObjectProperties / SHMultiFileProperties) without building the shell context menu, so it appears without the delay that loading shell extensions would add. The context-menu properties verb is only used as a fallback for exotic locations.

System requirements

Windows 11 24H2 / 25H2 or newer, with the WinAppSDK (WinUI 3) File Explorer command bar. Older versions (Windows 10, Windows 11 23H2 and earlier) use a completely different command bar; the mod stays silently disabled there.

How it works

The mod hooks a couple of functions of File Explorer's own WinUI 3 code (FileExplorerExtensions.dll), gets the command bar from there, and inserts a WinRT-constructed AppBarButton into its PrimaryCommands. The button survives tab switches, navigation and new windows, and is cleanly removed when the mod is disabled. Clicks drive the shell lookups from a worker thread, so the Explorer UI stays responsive.

File Explorer windows which were already open when the mod is enabled are handled too, but if the button doesn't show up in one of them right away, opening a new tab or navigating to another folder makes it appear.

Implementation follows the Explorer Command Bar mod by DanRotaru from the official windhawk-mods repository.

资源管理器属性按钮（中文说明）

在 Windows 11 文件资源管理器的命令栏（工具栏）上，"删除"和"排序"按钮之间添加一个"属性"按钮，点击后打开当前选中项目的属性对话框：

  • 支持多选：多选时与右键菜单里的"属性"一样，打开合并的属性对话框。
  • 支持虚拟位置：此电脑、回收站、Quick Access 等没有文件系统路径的项目也能正确打开属性。
  • 没有选中项时（可配置）：显示当前文件夹的属性，或什么都不做。

属性对话框通过快速 Shell API（SHObjectProperties / SHMultiFileProperties）直接打开，不构建右键菜单，避免了加载 shell 扩展带来的延迟；右键菜单的"属性"动词仅作为特殊位置的兜底。

系统要求

适用于 Windows 11 24H2 / 25H2 及以上使用 WinAppSDK (WinUI 3) 命令栏的文件资源管理器。旧版本（Windows 10、Windows 11 23H2 及更早）使用完全不同的命令栏实现，本 mod 会在其中安静地保持不启用状态。

工作原理

本 mod hook 了文件资源管理器自身的 WinUI 3 代码（FileExplorerExtensions.dll）中的若干函数，从那里拿到命令栏，并把一个用 WinRT 构造的 AppBarButton 插入 PrimaryCommands；按钮在切换标签页、导航、新窗口后自动恢复，禁用 mod 时被干净移除。点击的 Shell 查询由独立工作线程驱动，资源管理器界面保持响应。

启用本 mod 时已经打开的文件资源管理器窗口也会被处理；若某个已有窗口中按钮没有立即出现，打开一个新标签页或导航到其他文件夹即可让它出现。

实现参考了官方仓库的 Explorer Command Bar mod（DanRotaru），在此致谢。

entry.title: Win+V Panel Tweaks 1.0.0
entry.content:
Win+V Panel Tweaks

The Win+V clipboard panel and the Win+. emoji panel are the same panel, with tabs for Most recently used, Emoji, GIF, Kaomoji, Symbols and Clipboard. This mod makes the panel bigger or smaller and hides the tabs you turn off in its settings.

Panel size

The panel is normally 360 x 400 (in display-scaled pixels). Width and height are scaled separately, e.g. width 150% and height 100% gives 540 x 400. Windows still keeps the panel within the space available on screen. A new size applies the next time the panel opens.

By default the items keep their normal size, so a taller panel shows more clipboard entries and a wider one fits more emoji per row. Turn on "Scale content with the panel" to have the items grow with the panel instead.

Tabs

The Clipboard tab is always kept. Hiding a tab only removes its button: a shortcut that opens a view directly still opens it (e.g. Win+. still opens Emoji even when the Emoji tab is hidden).

How it works

The panel is drawn by TextInputHost.exe. Its size is computed in InputApp.dll, which the mod hooks using Microsoft's public symbols, so the first start after installing may take a moment while Windhawk downloads them.

The tab strip lives in a web page hosted in a WebView inside the panel. The same hook finds that WebView each time the panel opens and runs a small script in the page, which marks the chosen tabs as hidden in the page's own view model, re-applying it whenever the page resets them. Tweaks therefore show up the next time the panel opens after the mod is enabled.

That page ships with Windows but Microsoft can update it separately. If it changes in a way the mod doesn't recognize, the mod leaves it alone and the panel keeps working as usual.

Tested on Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200).

Source and research notes: https://github.com/jayll1303/WindowsClipboardMods

entry.title: Taskbar Audio Flipper 1.0.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Audio Flipper

A taskbar widget, in the style of the Windows weather widget, for switching audio devices. It has up to three sections, which you can each show or hide:

  • Output: the active output device's icon, name and volume. Click it to switch to the next output (speakers → headset → monitor → …).
  • Input: the same for your microphone.
  • Webcam: the chosen webcam's name and whether it's on, with a camera icon. Click it to turn the webcam on or off.

On the Output and Input sections:

  • Hover: a flyout opens above it with the device's name, a volume slider, and the device icon as a mute button, like the Windows 11 volume flyout.
  • Left-click: switch to the next device.
  • Scroll: turn the volume (or microphone level) up or down.
  • Middle-click: mute / unmute.

After you change the output volume, the mod plays the Windows "Default Beep" ding at the new level, like Windows' own volume slider. Turn it off with Output → Ding when changing volume.

Anywhere on the widget, right-click for the menu and drag left or right to move it along the taskbar. The Output, Input and Webcam submenus each have a Show on taskbar switch for their section, and the settings for it: picking a device directly, which devices are in the click rotation, whether to switch the communications device too, and links to the Windows settings.

Devices are shown with the name and icon they have in the Windows Sound control panel. To change them, choose Rename or change device icons… in the Output or Input submenu, right-click a device, and choose Properties.

Webcam on/off

Turn it on under Webcam → Show on taskbar and pick the webcam to control in the same menu. The camera icon has a slash through it while the webcam is off; click it to switch. Windows has no way to rename a webcam, but Webcam → Rename… gives it a name to show on the widget.

Turning the webcam off works like Disable device in Device Manager: no app can use it until it's turned back on. It stays off after a restart, and after the mod is turned off or removed. To turn it back on without the mod, open Device Manager, find the webcam under Cameras (or Imaging devices), right-click it and choose Enable device.

Windows only lets administrators turn devices on and off, so each switch runs Microsoft's PnP Utility (pnputil.exe) as administrator, which may show a Windows prompt asking to allow it, depending on your User Account Control settings.

Linking with Taskbar RDP Launcher

With the Taskbar RDP Launcher mod running too, the two widgets can be joined into one: right-click either, choose Link with RDPLauncher (or Link with AudioFlipper) and which side it goes on. Linked, they sit side by side with a divider between them, dragging either moves both, and if one hides the other takes its place.

Settings

The sections, the click rotation and the webcam settings are kept in the mod's storage, which Windhawk removes along with the mod. The first time it runs, the mod takes on the settings of the AudioFlipper app, if you have it (from %APPDATA%\AudioFlipper\settings.txt, which it doesn't change). Use the app or the mod, not both: each shows its own widget.

entry.title: Taskbar RDP Launcher 1.0.0
entry.content:
Taskbar RDP Launcher

A taskbar widget, in the style of the Windows weather widget, that starts Remote Desktop full screen on as many of your displays as you want. Instead of editing use multimon and selectedmonitors in an .rdp file (after looking up the display numbers with mstsc /l), click a number.

  • Number buttons: click 1, 2 or 3 to connect full screen on that many displays. There's one button for each display you have.
  • Hover a number to see a map of your displays, laid out the way they are on your desk. The ones that button uses are highlighted, and the session's main display (where the remote taskbar goes) has a bar along its bottom. Click a display to add it or take it off.
  • The computer shows its address, or the name you gave it over its address. Click it (or scroll over it) to go to the next of your computers.
  • Right-click for the menu: add computers (by name, from a saved .rdp file, or from Remote Desktop Connection's recent list), rename or remove them, and open their Remote Desktop settings.
  • Drag the widget left or right to move it along the taskbar.

Out of the box, 1 is your main display, 2 adds the display nearest to it, and so on up to all of them. The buttons are remembered for each arrangement of displays, so a laptop that's sometimes docked keeps separate buttons for the desk and for the road.

How it connects

  • Computers added by name connect with mstsc /v:<computer>, like typing the computer into Remote Desktop Connection. Since the April 2026 Windows update, Remote Desktop shows a security warning every time an .rdp file is opened, but not for computers typed in, so this avoids it.

    Remote Desktop Connection takes the display options for these from its own settings file, Default.rdp in Documents. So just before the session starts, the mod sets screen mode id, use multimon, span monitors and selectedmonitors there (creating the file, hidden, if there isn't one), and as soon as the session ends, it puts back what they were. It notes what they were in its own storage first, so if Windhawk is closed during a session, they're put back the next time the mod starts; if the mod is turned off during a session, they're put back right away. A setting you change in Remote Desktop Connection in the meantime is left as you set it.

  • Saved .rdp files are never changed: the mod opens a copy with the display options set (and gets the warning, as any .rdp file does), and deletes the copy when the session ends. If the file is signed and its signature covers the display options, the copy goes without the signature, so Remote Desktop shows it as from an unknown publisher.

  • Remote Desktop numbers displays its own way (not as Windows Settings does), so the first time you connect on some of your displays, the mod reads Remote Desktop's list (mstsc /l, whose box may flash) and remembers it until your displays change. Read display numbers again in the menu asks again.

Linking with Taskbar Audio Flipper

With the Taskbar Audio Flipper mod running too, the two widgets can be joined into one: right-click either, choose Link with AudioFlipper (or Link with RDPLauncher) and which side it goes on. Linked, they sit side by side with a divider between them, dragging either moves both, and if one hides the other takes its place.

Settings

The computers, their names and the display buttons are kept in the mod's storage, which Windhawk removes along with the mod. The first time it runs, the mod takes on the computers and display buttons of the RDPLauncher app, if you have it (from %APPDATA%\RDPLauncher\settings.txt, which it doesn't change). Use the app or the mod, not both: each shows its own widget.

entry.title: Mawaqit Prayer Clock 0.6.9
entry.content:
Mawaqit Prayer Clock

Mawaqit prayer clock with live countdown, prayer schedule popup, and customizable themes.

Features

  • Upcoming prayer name, scheduled time, and live countdown
  • Clickable prayer-schedule popup with optional auto-close timer
  • 13 appearance themes, including Windows / System, Traditional Islamic, Catppuccin Mocha, Emberveil, Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox Dark, Tokyo Night, Solarized Dark and Light, and Custom
  • Independent custom colors for the pill and popup
  • Visibility switches for the prayer label, countdown, and popup
  • Five selectable taskbar positions, including experimental dynamic centering
  • Native XAML taskbar integration with reserved layout space for anchored positions
  • Automatic or manual clock height, four-sided margins and padding, tray gap, corner radius, and font size
  • Background schedule updates through native WinHTTP, with configurable refresh interval
  • Live settings updates without restarting Explorer

Network access and cached schedules

This mod intentionally uses Mawaqit’s published mosque-specific prayer times rather than locally calculated astronomical times, preserving mosque-specific adjustments.

This mod connects to https://mawaqit.net over HTTPS to retrieve the public prayer schedule for the mosque identifier configured in Settings. The request is an HTTP GET for https://mawaqit.net/<language>/<mosque-identifier>; no account or authentication is required. The server can observe the request and normal connection information such as your IP address.

The schedule is stored in Windhawk's mod-specific storage. A valid cached schedule is reused when Explorer restarts, until the configured refresh interval expires (24 hours by default; adjustable from 1 to 168 hours). The mod also requests a fresh schedule when the mosque or refresh interval changes. If a download fails, it retries after one hour. An empty, expired, mismatched, or unusable cache causes a download at startup. The mod reads schedule data from the public Mawaqit webpage, so changes to that page can interrupt updates.

Screenshots

Mawaqit Prayer Clock supports multiple appearance themes to match your Windows 11 desktop.

Windows System Default | Traditional Islamic | |:---:|:---:| | |

| Catppuccin Mocha | Emberveil | |:---:|:---:| | | |

Desktop Integration

See how Mawaqit Prayer Clock integrates into a fully customized Windows 11 desktop.

Configuration

Choose a mosque identifier or Mawaqit URL in Settings. Select an appearance theme and customize the widget as desired. Custom color settings only apply when the Custom theme is selected. Set popup auto-close to 0 to keep the popup open until dismissed.

More information

For installation instructions, additional screenshots, troubleshooting, and release information, visit:

GitHub Project

Compatibility and credits

Windows 11 only. Taskbar XAML integration adapted from Windhawk’s taskbar-folder-menus (MIT).

License

MIT License.

Disclaimer

This is an unofficial community project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Mawaqit.

entry.title: Maximized Window Margins 1.0
entry.content:
Maximized Window Margins

Maximized windows no longer touch the screen edges. A configurable gap is kept on every side, which pairs nicely with a floating dock (for example the Luminosity or DockLike themes of Windows 11 Taskbar Styler).

How it works

The mod runs as a tool mod (in its own windhawk.exe process, nothing is injected into other programs). For each monitor and each edge with a margin greater than zero, it registers an invisible AppBar of the configured thickness. Windows then reduces the work area, and every maximized window fits inside it.

  • Margins are set in DIPs and scaled per monitor DPI.
  • AppBars are registered again when Explorer restarts, when displays change, and when the taskbar or another AppBar moves.
  • Disabling the mod restores the original work area immediately.

Side effects

Since the work area itself shrinks, the gap also applies to:

  • Snap / Snap Layouts (snapped windows keep the margin too).
  • Desktop icon placement.
  • Anything else that positions itself from the work area, such as pop-ups and notifications that apps place in a corner of the screen.

Real fullscreen apps (games, videos, F11) cover the whole monitor and are not affected.

Tips

  • With a floating dock, the taskbar still reserves its own height at the bottom. The bottom margin is added on top of it, so a small value (0–10) is usually enough.
  • Maximized windows have square corners in Windows 11. To round them, install Custom Window Corner Radius and set "Rounded corners for maximized and snapped windows" to "Round snapped and maximized windows". The "Corner radius" setting of that mod then applies to maximized windows too.

entry.title: Disable Windows Audio Limiter 1.0
entry.content:
Disable Windows Audio Limiter

Windows has a built-in audio adjustment mechanism that decreases the volume for a few seconds after a loud click or increases if a video or audio has dropped volume. This mod disables this adjustment.

After mod start, restart the Windows audio service, executing with admin privileges:

net stop audiosrv

net start audiosrv

or reboot.

entry.title: BubbleGlass Screensaver 1.7.6
entry.content:
BubbleGlass Screensaver

A transparent, animated soap-bubble screensaver for the Windows desktop.

BubbleGlass shows colorful, iridescent soap bubbles directly above the live Windows desktop after a period of inactivity. The desktop stays visible and live underneath (per-pixel alpha layered window), and any keyboard or mouse activity dismisses the saver instantly. Rendering targets smooth 60 FPS even on large multi-monitor desktops.

Preview

Soap bubbles drifting over the live Windows desktop. The optional diagnostics overlay shows real-time FPS, frame time, jitter and rendering performance.

Features

  • Transparent overlay above the live desktop - wallpaper, windows and video remain visible underneath.
  • Smooth 60 FPS animation with QPC-based frame pacing and motion timing.
  • Thin-film iridescent bubbles: rainbow interference arcs, membrane rim, specular highlight, hotspot and a faint opposite-side reflection.
  • Organic wobble, slowly changing interference colors, optional subtle shadow.
  • Gradual spawning, size variation, natural drift and optional turbulence.
  • Bubble-to-bubble collisions (lightly damped) plus wall bouncing or edge wrapping.
  • Configurable lifetime with an animated pop effect (expansion, flash, expanding ring).
  • Primary-monitor or full multi-monitor mode.
  • Instant dismissal on keystroke, click, mouse wheel or mouse movement (with a small movement threshold). Input is never swallowed.
  • Fullscreen video playback (including fullscreen browser video) is intentionally supported: bubbles remain above the live, moving video.
  • Windows presentation mode is suppressed when reported by Windows. Other fullscreen states are not automatically blocked to preserve video playback.
  • Hidden automatically while the session is locked, disconnected or the display is off.
  • Optional on-screen performance diagnostics and Windhawk/DbgView logging.
  • No permanent clock or date elements.

How It Works

BubbleGlass watches keyboard/mouse idle time. After the configured timeout it creates a click-through, topmost layered window and composites premultiplied-per-pixel-alpha bubbles over the desktop with UpdateLayeredWindowIndirect. Bubbles are drawn with GDI+ into per-bubble sprites that are cached and refreshed on a small time budget; only changed areas are cleared and presented (dirty rectangles). Low-level input hooks run on a dedicated thread and only while the saver is visible.

Performance

The renderer targets 60 FPS; actual speed depends on resolution, bubble count and bubble sizes. The largest tuning levers are bubble count, maximum bubble size, sprite refresh interval, iridescence and total desktop area.

Enable Show internal performance stats for the FPS / frame-time / jitter overlay, and Log performance stats to Windhawk/DbgView for one summary line per second. Every option (timeout, bubble count and size, motion, physics, lifetime, pop, appearance, performance, diagnostics) is described in the settings UI.

Usage

  1. Install and enable the BubbleGlass Screensaver mod.
  2. Configure the inactivity timeout and appearance.
  3. Leave the computer idle; BubbleGlass appears automatically.
  4. Move the mouse or press a key to dismiss it.

No separate .scr screensaver file is required.

Notes

  • BubbleGlass intentionally keeps the Windows desktop visible underneath; it is not a full-screen scene replacement like classic screensavers.
  • The dismissing keystroke or click is also delivered to the focused application (input is never swallowed).
  • Fullscreen video is intentionally allowed. Automatic suppression of every fullscreen app would also block this core feature. Windows presentation mode is suppressed when detectable; gamepad-only input may not reset Windows idle time, so fullscreen games are not guaranteed to suppress the saver.
  • BubbleGlass never appears while the session is locked or display is off.
  • Bubble sizes and the diagnostics overlay use raw pixels (no DPI scaling).
  • "Span all monitors" uses the virtual-screen bounding rectangle; on mixed-size or offset monitor layouts parts of that rectangle may not be on any display.

Compatibility

Designed for Windows 11 and Windhawk. Runs as a dedicated Windhawk tool-mod process - no .scr screensaver file and no winlogon injection. Rendering uses standard GDI/GDI+ and layered-window APIs (no DirectX or GPU API).

Credits

Developed and tested by SilverAmd, with iterative performance analysis, profiling and optimization focused on smooth frame pacing, large desktop resolutions, multi-monitor support and low rendering overhead.

entry.title: Fancy Task View Cross-Monitor Drag 0.7.0
entry.content:
Fancy Task View Cross-Monitor Drag

Move windows between monitors by dragging their thumbnails in Windows 11 Task View (Win + Tab).

Features

  • Drag a Task View window thumbnail from one monitor to another.
  • Remember window size and position separately for each monitor.
  • Configure first-time window sizing and positioning.
  • Choose whether Task View stays open, closes, or closes and reopens after a move.

Limitations

  • Task View may continue displaying the original thumbnail placement until reopened.
  • Virtual desktop assignments do not change.
  • Elevated or protected windows may not accept movement requests.
  • Some applications adjust their own dimensions when changing monitors.
  • Window positions are remembered while the mod is running.
  • Windows with duplicate titles on the source monitor cannot be identified.
  • A thumbnail whose name differs from its window title cannot be identified.

entry.title: Windows 8/8.1 Display Switch Recreation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 8/8.1 Display Switch Recreation

IMPORTANT: This modification runs in explorer.exe and does not require adding the critical dwm.exe process to Windhawk's inclusion list. When an elevated window or a secure desktop is active, Windows may not deliver keyboard input to Explorer; in that case the native Project flyout remains available.

This mod recreates the Windows 8/8.1 display switch panel (the Second screen flyout in Windows 8 and the Project pane in Windows 8.1) on Windows 10 and Windows 11. It uses the real Windows display configuration and does not replace system files, patch the graphics driver, or modify native display binaries. Topology changes and Set as main display use documented Windows APIs and persist like the native Project flyout. This modification has been tested on Windows 10 21H2 and Windows 11 24H2.

Screenshot

Features

  • Four native display modes: PC screen only, Duplicate, Extend, and Second screen only.
  • Live display state with monitor hotplug and Settings-app changes reflected while the panel is open.
  • Windows 8.1-style layout, embedded icons, accent color, per-monitor DPI support, and translations for English, Italian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, German, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
  • Right-click commands: Set as main display, Detect displays, More settings, and Copy monitor information.
  • Keyboard controls: Win+P to open or toggle, Left/Right/Up/Down to select, Enter or Space to apply, 1-4 for direct selection, F5 to detect displays, and Esc to dismiss.
  • While the panel is open, repeated Win+P presses cycle through the modes; releasing Win applies the selected mode and closes the panel.
  • Click-outside and foreground-change dismissal, plus a status line for display API errors.
  • The Windows 8/8.1 Devices > Second screen/Project route and a no-argument DisplaySwitch.exe launch replace the native DisplaySwitchUIWnd; direct commands such as DisplaySwitch.exe /extend remain untouched.

Win+P input path

When enabled, the mod installs one narrow WH_KEYBOARD_LL hook in the main explorer.exe process. It consumes only the physical Win+P sequence, passes injected input and every other key through, and sends private messages to the panel. The hook is removed when the setting is disabled or the mod is unloaded. If an elevated window or a secure desktop is active, the hook may not receive the input; the native Windows Project flyout is intentionally preserved in that case.

The panel loads only in the Explorer process that owns the shell window, so separate folder-window processes do not create duplicate panels.

Windows APIs

The panel uses documented public APIs:

| Purpose | API | | --- | --- | | Read paths, topology, and monitor names | QueryDisplayConfig, GetDisplayConfigBufferSizes, DisplayConfigGetDeviceInfo | | Apply or validate a topology | SetDisplayConfig with SDC_APPLY, SDC_VALIDATE, and the topology flags | | Detect displays | SetDisplayConfig with SDC_USE_DATABASE_CURRENT | | Set the primary display | ChangeDisplaySettingsEx with CDS_SET_PRIMARY and CDS_UPDATEREGISTRY | | Monitor information and DPI | EnumDisplayMonitors, GetMonitorInfo, EnumDisplaySettingsEx, GetDpiForMonitor | | Other display settings | ms-settings:display deep links | | Replace another native Project flyout | SetWinEventHook(EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND) and DisplaySwitchUIWnd detection | | Error reporting | documented return codes and FormatMessage |

The mod does not write arbitrary registry values, call driver-private interfaces, launch DisplaySwitch.exe, or undo user-requested display changes when disabled. ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED is shown in the panel when the current session cannot change the display configuration.

Settings

  • Open with Win+P: replace the native Project flyout and supported native entry points.
  • Panel color: accent, Charcoal, or Custom color.
  • Full-height pane: use the Windows 8.1 full-height layout or fit the content.
  • Validate before applying: validate the topology with SDC_VALIDATE before applying it.
  • Allow path persistence: add SDC_PATH_PERSIST_IF_REQUIRED when applying a topology.
  • Disable unavailable options: gray out modes that require more than one connected display.

Limitations

  • The mod cannot make a topology work when the display driver does not support it.
  • Wireless-display discovery remains part of the native Windows Connect experience.
  • Resolution, refresh rate, orientation, HDR, and the embedded artwork are not re-created or changed.

Credits

  • AdministratoX — Metro UI interface template.
  • Meteoni — IsMainExplorerProcess pattern.
  • The Windows 8/8.1 Search Charm Recreation mod — panel, animation, light dismiss, z-band, context-menu, and translation components.

entry.title: Micrographics Taskbar Clock 1.0
entry.content:
Micrographics Taskbar Clock

Replaces the Windows 11 taskbar clock with a clock face inspired by the "Micrographics" clock of Nothing OS 5.

  • Weekday, day of month in a filled pill, month in an outlined pill, the time and a block cursor.
  • Temperature, a weather icon and the current conditions in a speech bubble.
  • Follows the taskbar's light/dark text color automatically, on every monitor.
  • Clicking the clock still opens the notification center and calendar.

Weather

The weather line is off by default, and the mod makes no network requests until it's turned on. To show it, enable Show weather in the settings and enter a city name or latitude,longitude as the location. Weather then comes from Open-Meteo (free, no API key), and a city name is looked up with Open-Meteo's geocoding service.

Alternatively, enable Detect location from IP address to leave the location empty. Your public IP address is then sent to ipwho.is, or to GeoJS if that fails, to approximate your location.

Fonts

The default font is Bahnschrift, which ships with Windows. Any installed font can be used, e.g. a monospaced one such as Cascadia Mono, or a dot matrix font.

Other clock mods

This mod hides the original clock text and draws its own clock face, so changes from other clock mods, such as Taskbar Clock Customization, aren't visible while it's enabled.

entry.title: Windows Terminal Start Minimized 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows Terminal Start Minimized

English | Português

Made in Brazil by caliberda · bugs and ideas: an issue on GitHub · Instagram @cesar.kali · caliberda.com.br

When Windows Terminal opens at sign-in, this mod makes it start minimized, or straight in the notification area, instead of on the screen.

Required: turn on Terminal's options

The mod works through Terminal's own options and never changes them, so it does nothing until you turn them on. Open Terminal's settings (Ctrl+,):

  1. Required: Startup > Launch on machine startup (called Launch at login in newer versions). Microsoft's guide. Terminal must also be on in Windows Settings > Apps > Startup.
  2. To start in the notification area: Appearance > Hide Terminal in the notification area when it is minimized. Microsoft's guide. Without it, Terminal starts minimized on the taskbar.

Then sign out and back in (or restart) to see it work.

What changes

Without the mod, Terminal opens on the screen at sign-in even with both options on, and only goes to the notification area after you minimize it. With the mod:

  • With option 2 on, it goes straight to the notification area, without showing on the screen.
  • With option 2 off, it starts minimized on the taskbar.

It doesn't take the focus from what you're doing. Click its icon to bring it back, in the size Terminal would have used (maximized, if Terminal is set to launch maximized).

How it works

The mod runs only inside Windows Terminal. When Windows starts Terminal through its Launch on machine startup option, the windows of that launch (one, or one per window when Terminal restores your last session) are shown minimized instead of on the screen. Opening Terminal any other way (Start menu, taskbar, wt command, a shortcut) isn't changed, even right after you sign in.

The mod stops acting when you bring back one of those windows, or one minute after Terminal started.

Known limitations

  • Only the Microsoft Store (packaged) version of Terminal has the Launch on machine startup option. The portable (zip) version is left unchanged.
  • If Windhawk starts after Terminal, the mod can't act on that sign-in.

Contact

I'm caliberda, a developer from Brazil. Write in English, Portuguese or your own language.

  • Bugs and ideas: an issue on GitHub, the best way: report a bug or suggest an idea. It mentions me (@cesarkali), so I see it.
  • Instagram @cesar.kali: to talk to me and follow my projects.
  • caliberda.com.br: my site, with my other projects and a Discord link.

Português

Feito no Brasil por caliberda · pode falar comigo em português · bugs e ideias: uma issue no GitHub · Instagram @cesar.kali · caliberda.com.br

Quando o Windows Terminal abre no logon, este mod faz ele já iniciar minimizado, ou direto na área de notificação, em vez de aparecer na tela.

Obrigatório: ligue as opções do Terminal

O mod funciona pelas opções do próprio Terminal e nunca as altera, então ele não faz nada até você ligá-las. Abra as configurações do Terminal (Ctrl+,):

  1. Obrigatório: Inicialização > Iniciar na inicialização da máquina (chamada Iniciar no logon nas versões mais novas). Guia da Microsoft. O Terminal também precisa estar ligado em Configurações do Windows > Aplicativos > Inicialização.
  2. Para iniciar na área de notificação: Aparência > Ocultar o Terminal na área de notificação quando estiver minimizado. Guia da Microsoft. Sem ela, o Terminal inicia minimizado na barra de tarefas.

Depois, saia da conta e entre de novo (ou reinicie) para ver funcionando.

O que muda

Sem o mod, o Terminal abre na tela no logon mesmo com as duas opções ligadas, e só vai para a área de notificação depois que você o minimiza. Com o mod:

  • Com a opção 2 ligada, ele vai direto para a área de notificação, sem aparecer na tela.
  • Com a opção 2 desligada, ele inicia minimizado na barra de tarefas.

Ele não tira o foco do que você está fazendo. Clique no ícone dele para trazê-lo de volta, no tamanho que o Terminal usaria (maximizado, se o Terminal estiver configurado para abrir maximizado).

Como funciona

O mod roda só dentro do Windows Terminal. Quando o Windows abre o Terminal pela opção Iniciar na inicialização da máquina, as janelas dessa inicialização (uma, ou uma por janela quando o Terminal restaura a última sessão) aparecem minimizadas em vez de na tela. Abrir o Terminal de outro jeito (menu Iniciar, barra de tarefas, comando wt, um atalho) não muda, mesmo logo depois de você entrar.

O mod para de agir quando você traz de volta uma dessas janelas, ou um minuto depois de o Terminal iniciar.

Limitações conhecidas

  • Só a versão da Microsoft Store (empacotada) do Terminal tem a opção Iniciar na inicialização da máquina. A versão portátil (zip) não muda.
  • Se o Windhawk iniciar depois do Terminal, o mod não consegue agir naquele logon.

Contato

Sou o caliberda, desenvolvedor brasileiro. Pode escrever em português.

  • Bugs e ideias: uma issue no GitHub, o melhor caminho: relatar um bug ou sugerir uma ideia. Ela já me marca (@cesarkali), então eu vejo.
  • Instagram @cesar.kali: para conversar comigo e acompanhar meus projetos.
  • caliberda.com.br: meu site, com meus outros projetos e um link para o Discord.

entry.title: Audio Hardware Volume Preset 1.3.0
entry.content:
Audio Hardware Volume Preset

Automatically sets your headphones, speakers, Bluetooth headsets, USB DACs, or any other audio playback hardware to a specific preset volume whenever they connect.

Key Features

  • Prevent Sudden Hearing Blasts: Never plug in headphones only to be blasted by 100% volume again.
  • Smart Hardware Matching: Supports flexible keyword and token matching. You can enter simple keywords (like AirPods, Sony, DAC, Speakers) or full device names.
  • Max Volume Safety Cap: Set a ceiling on the preset volume applied at connect time (up to 100%).
  • Global Fallback: Set any unrecognized audio device to a safe default volume (e.g., 30%).
  • Auto-Unmute: Optionally unmute the device on connection.
  • Intelligent Debouncing: Prevents duplicate triggers when Windows fires multiple rapid connection events.
  • Safe & Efficient: Runs as a dedicated background tool mod using standard Windows Core Audio event notifications (IMMNotificationClient). Zero polling, zero idle CPU usage.
